topics.name: Adverbs of manner, place and time

options: Meera spoke politely to the nurse.
Meera spoke polite to the nurse.
Meera spoke politeness to the nurse.
questions.rule: To tell how she spoke, use the adverb of manner politely.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: Grandfather was sitting on the mat.
Grandfather were sitting on the mat.
Grandfather was sit on the mat.
questions.rule: Past continuous = was/were + verb-ing. One person takes was: was sitting.

options: Charaka was a man of great kind.
Charaka was a man of great kindness.
Charaka was a man of great kindly.
questions.rule: After of great we need a noun. kind + ness = kindness.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: To say how he cleaned it, use the adverb carefully, not the adjective careful.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Past continuous needs was + verb-ing: was playing.
Comparing two things with than needs the comparative: older.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct adverb of time.
questions.rule: will call is about the future, so the time adverb must be future: tomorrow.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence in the past continuous.
questions.rule: Subject + was + verb-ing + object: Meera was spinning a wooden top.

chat: How did the old doctor speak to his patients?
options: He spoke to them very gentle.
He spoke to them very gently.
He speaked to them very gently.
questions.rule: How? needs an adverb of manner: gently. The past of speak is spoke.

chat: Which is better for a cough, cold milk or ginger tea?
options: Ginger tea is best than cold milk.
questions.rule: good - better - best. Never say more better; use better for two things.

options: Charaka was one of the greatest physicians of ancient India.
Charaka was one of the most greatest physicians of ancient India.
Charaka was one of the great physician of ancient India.
questions.rule: Never use most with -est. one of the greatest + plural noun: physicians.

options: Regular exercise helps in the prevention of illness.
Regular exercise helps in the prevent of illness.
Regular exercise helps in the preventive of illness.
questions.rule: After the we need a noun: prevent + ion = prevention.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After a careful we need a noun: examine + ation = examination.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: How did we wait? Use the adverb of manner patiently.
children is plural and the time is past, so use were laughing.
After with we need a noun: wonder. Wonderful is an adjective, wonderfully an adverb.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence with an adverb of place.
questions.rule: upstairs tells us where. It is an adverb of place.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence with a superlative.
questions.rule: Comparing with a whole group uses the + superlative: the youngest.

chat: What were you doing when the lights went out?
questions.rule: The question is in the past continuous, so answer with I was reading.

chat: Why do you like Dr. Joshi so much?
options: She treats every patient with kind.
She treats every patient with kindness.
She treat every patient with kindness.
questions.rule: After with use the noun kindness; she takes treats.
yesterday is an adverb of past time, so the verb must be past: finished.

options: Turmeric paste is usefuller than ginger for a wound.
Turmeric paste is more useful than ginger for a wound.
Turmeric paste is most useful than ginger for a wound.
questions.rule: Long adjectives like useful take more with than: more useful than.

options: While Grandfather was telling the story, Meera were listening.
While Grandfather telling the story, Meera was listening.
While Grandfather was telling the story, Meera was listening.
questions.rule: Two actions going on together use past continuous: was telling ... was listening.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: care and ___ joins two nouns, so use the noun compassion.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: than needs the comparative form: faster than.
To tell how he picked her up, use the adverb quickly.
good is irregular: good - better - best. With than, use better.
Past continuous question: Wh-word + were + subject + verb-ing?

chat: How often do you practise cricket?
questions.rule: A habit takes the simple present I practise, and every is followed by a singular noun.

chat: How was your visit to the herbal garden?
options: It was very useful and enjoyment.
It was very useful and enjoyable.
It was very use and enjoyable.
questions.rule: After was very we need adjectives: use + ful, enjoy + able.

options: An old banyan tree sways gently in the breeze.
A old banyan tree sways gently in the breeze.
An old banyan tree sways gentle in the breeze.
questions.rule: an before a vowel sound (an old), and the adverb gently tells how it sways.

options: Charaka's book is one of the oldest books on medicine.
Charaka's book are one of the oldest books on medicine.
Charaka's book is one of the oldest book on medicine.
questions.rule: book is singular, so is; one of the oldest takes a plural noun: books.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After was, the past continuous needs verb-ing: was shining.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Doctor Rao is one person, so the simple present takes -s: speaks. softly is the adverb.

questions.after: tying a bandage when the phone rang.
questions.rule: An action in progress when another happened: was tying (one person, past).
useful begins with a 'yoo' sound, so use a, not an: a useful remedy.
grateful for + noun. kindness is the noun made with the suffix -ness.
Yes/no question in past continuous: Were + you + verb-ing ... ?

chat: Did you drink your ginger tea?
options: Yes, I did drank it slowly.
questions.rule: The past of drink is drank; slowly tells how.

chat: Who is the tallest boy in your class?
options: Arjun is the taller boy in our class.
Arjun is the tallest boy in our class.
Arjun is tallest boy than all in our class.
questions.rule: Comparing one with the whole class needs the tallest.

options: A good doctor must be wise, compassion and deeply observant.
A good doctor must be wise, compassionate and deep observant.
A good doctor must be wise, compassionate and deeply observant.
questions.rule: After be we list adjectives (compassionate); the adverb deeply describes the adjective observant.

options: The more carefully you listen, the more you learn.
The more careful you listen, the more you learn.
The most carefully you listen, the more you learn.
questions.rule: listen needs an adverb (carefully), and the pattern is the more ..., the more ....

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The long action takes past continuous (was running); the sudden action takes simple past: fell.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: most ___ healers needs an adjective: compassion + ate = compassionate.

questions.after: than many modern systems of medicine.
questions.rule: much + comparative + than: much older than. Short adjectives take -er, not more.
To tell how she examined it, use the adverb thoroughly.
the greatest + noun + of + group is the superlative pattern.
Why + was + subject + verb-ing; so loudly tells how she cried.

chat: My grandmother puts turmeric on small cuts.
options: Yes, it heals them more quicker than plain water.
Yes, it heal them more quickly than plain water.
Yes, it heals them more quickly than plain water.
questions.rule: The adverb quickly compares with more quickly; it takes heals.

chat: What were you and Priya doing in the library at noon?
options: We was reading about Indian scientists.
We were read about Indian scientists.
We were reading about Indian scientists.
questions.rule: We takes were, and past continuous needs verb-ing: were reading.
